questions.question: If unsure whether a road is becoming icy, a driver can:

options.text: Open the window and feel the front of the mirror for ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and feel the front of the mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road may be icy, open your window and feel the front of your side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice is on these items, the road is likely icy too.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of jackknifing by:
questions.explanation: Prevent skidding by steering, speeding up, and braking smoothly. If your drive wheels or trailer wheels skid on a tank vehicle, the vehicle may jackknife.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be checked:

options.text: To make sure they are clear.
To make sure they connect to the battery.
To make sure they have the right amount of slack.

questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle with power steering, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Most importantly, check the hoses for leaks.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Is a major cause of deadly crashes.
Can help you reach your destination faster.
Should only be done on dry roads.
Is okay when traffic is light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of deadly crashes.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of deadly crashes. Never drive faster than the speed limit and adjust your speed for road conditions.

questions.question: If a trailer is too high:

options.text: It will not matter when coupling.
The coupling will be more secure.

questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, make sure the trailer is at the right height. If the trailer is too low, the trailer nose may be damaged. If it is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up.
Allow all wheels to lock up.
Help prevent wheels from locking up.
Alert other drivers when you are braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help prevent wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops the wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: If a tire rim is damaged, it should be:

options.text: Moved to the axle farthest from the driver.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are not safe and must be replaced.

questions.question: The best way to know if your trailer is skidding is by:
questions.explanation: The earliest and best way to detect a trailer skid is to see the trailer drift off-course in your mirrors.

questions.question: A fully-loaded tank vehicle:

options.text: Needs less room to stop than an empty vehicle.
Needs more room to stop than a partially-loaded vehicle.
Needs the same room to stop as an empty vehicle.
Stops faster on a wet road than on a dry road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needs less room to stop than an empty vehicle.
questions.explanation: Empty tank vehicles often need more space to stop than fully-loaded tank vehicles. Wet roads double stopping distance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tire problem to check for and avoid?

options.text: Recapped tires on the front of a school bus.
All tires are made by the same company.

questions.correctAnswerText: All tires are made by the same company.
questions.explanation: During an inspection, check for many tire problems: wrong air pressure; excessive wear; cuts or damage; tread separation; dual tires touching each other or other parts; mismatched sizes; mixed radial and bias-ply tires; cut or cracked valve stems; and regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires on school bus front wheels. The manufacturer of the tires is not a concern.

questions.question: If your trailer moves off course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward, adjust your position, and back up again.
Get out and push the trailer into the correct position.
Turn the steering wheel all the way left until the trailer straightens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward, adjust your position, and back up again.
questions.explanation: If your trailer moves off course while backing, move forward and reposition your vehicle before backing up again.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: When standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before starting a trip. On a vehicle with a trailer, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: What affects stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Speed affects stopping distance. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers. Directions are not.

questions.question: A driver should always:

options.text: Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Watch the road constantly for hazards. Plan ahead for how to handle dangerous situations if they happen.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer will likely swing around.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will likely swing around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer tends to swing around. This can cause a jackknife.

questions.question: Why can tanks with baffles still roll over?

options.text: Baffles add too much weight to the tank.
The liquid can surge side to side.
Drivers usually don't know about the baffles.
Baffles can become uneven and tip the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: The liquid can surge side to side.
questions.explanation: Baffles stop forward and backward movement, but not side-to-side movement. Liquid surging to the sides can cause rollovers.

questions.question: Which is NOT another name for convex mirrors?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are also called "fisheye," "spot," or "bug-eye" mirrors. Flat side mirrors are not convex mirrors.

questions.question: What letters show that a substance is in a reportable quantity?
questions.explanation: When a substance is in a reportable quantity, the shipper must show the letters "RQ" on the shipping paper and package.

questions.question: When do you need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: For a Class A license vehicle.
For a Class B license vehicle.
For a Class C license vehicle.

questions.explanation: You need a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials in any vehicle, regardless of size.
